title.narrative: IGAD: Regional Refugee management phase II

description.narrative: Stödet för IGAD:s andra fas kommer att bygga på de framsteg som gjorts i den första fasen, särskilt vad gäller utvecklingen, valideringen och godkännandet av IGAD:s policyramverk för flyktingskydd. Den andra fasens stöd kommer att fokusera på genomförandet av policyramverket med ett djupare samarbete med flyktingar, flyktingledda och kvinnoledda organisationer. Programmet kommer att tillhandahålla tekniskt stöd till medlemsstaterna i syfte att anpassa och harmonisera nationella strategier med det regionala policyramverket, samt stärka skyddsresponsen för flyktingar i regionen. Dessutom kommer programmet att stärka IGAD-medlemsstaternas kapacitet i processer för fastställande av flyktingstatus samt öka effektiviteten i dessa processer. 'Gender Equality' är markerat som ett viktigt mål för detta program, eftersom programmet kommer att genomföra en genusanalys och erbjuda utbildning till medlemsstaterna vad gäller olika genusaspekter i policyutveckling samt tillhandahålla tekniskt stöd för att integrera genuskänsliga element i flyktinghanteringspolicyers och strategier. Dessutom syftar programmet till att öka kvinnors och kvinnoledda organisationers deltagande i diskussioner om policyförändringar med beslutsfattare på nationell och subnationell nivå.

The IGAD second phase support will build on the progress made in the first phase support, specifically the development, validation, and endorsement of the IGAD Policy Framework on Refugee Protection. The second phase support will focus on the implementation of the policy framework with more engagement of refugees, refugee-led and women-led organizations. The program will provide technical assistance to MS to align national policies to the regional Policy framework, facilitating the harmonization of policies in the region as well as improving the refugee protection space in the region. Moreover, the program will strengthen the capacity of IGAD Member States in Refugee Status Determination (RSD) processes and aim to increase efficiency in these processes.
The program has marked 'Gender Equality' as a significant objective as the program will conduct a gender analysis, and provide technical assistance to Member States to revise national refugee management policies with gender considerations.
Furthermore, the program aims to enhance the participation of women and women-led organizations in policy change discussions with policy makers.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
1. The programme has supported the validation of the IGAD Policy Framework on Refugee Protection indicators for integration into the Consolidated Results Monitoring Framework. This provides IGAD and its Member States with a clearer and more harmonized basis for monitoring progress on refugee protection and contributes to maintaining an enabling policy environment in the region. Refugee participation in regional policy processes has been strengthened through the establishment of the Regional Refugee Engagement Forum (RREF), which offers a structured platform for engagement by refugee representatives and refugee-led organizations.
2. A comprehensive mapping of refugee-led organizations in the IGAD region has improved understanding of community level actors and their roles in displacement contexts. The programme has also facilitated knowledge exchange and documentation on the displacement impacts of the Sudanese conflict, contributing to more informed and context specific responses at local and national levels. In addition, a regional gender analysis has been developed and validated, and an associated workplan has been finalized.
3. An Institutional Capacity Needs Assessment of Member State refugee management agencies has provided a systematic overview of existing capacities and operational gaps. In Djibouti, targeted capacity strengthening for ONARS staff on Refugee Status Determination has supported efforts to reduce administrative backlogs and improve case processing. Collectively, these activities contribute to Member States ability to implement the IGAD Policy Framework and related regional mechanisms. Furthermore, regional and national technical working groups on migration and displacement statistics were strengthened, improving harmonization of definitions, methods, and tools across Member States. Twenty five experts were trained in refugee and IDP data management and analysis, supporting better national reporting aligned with international recommendations.
4. The programme has supported national multistakeholder dialogues focused on refugee inclusion and durable solutions. These engagements have facilitated coordination among national authorities, civil society organizations, and development and humanitarian partners, contributing to more coherent approaches to advancing durable solutions within Member States.
5. Regional coordination has been strengthened through structured engagement on statelessness commitments under the Global Refugee Forum (GRF), contributing to clearer follow-up mechanisms and improved information sharing among IGAD institutions and Member States. The programme's monitoring and documentation efforts have also supported more systematic planning and reporting at the regional level.
